主要内容: Sovereign wealth funds (SWFs) are increasingly investing in real estate amid volatile stock markets, according to an analyst. Michael Maduell, president of the Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute, noted that SWFs are seeking long-term investments where they can secure their capital without needing to reinvest frequently. The institute analyzes investments by public asset owners, including SWFs and other long-term governmental investors. Pension funds and endowments are also boosting their real estate and infrastructure investments. Norway's Government Pension Fund Global, the world's largest sovereign wealth fund with over $830 billion in assets under management (AUM), increased its real estate allocation and is exploring core property markets in Asia. Saudi Arabia unveiled a 15-year plan to transform its economy, with the country's sovereign wealth fund expected to grow from $200 billion in AUM to $6.5 trillion in March 2016. Preqin's research indicated that commodities funds have suffered due to the shift into real estate and other stable investments, with SWF holdings dropping 50% in March. Additionally, oil prices remaining low have led exporting countries to liquidate assets to fund government spending. Saudi Arabia also announced the listing of its state-owned oil company, Saudi Aramco, with plans to sell a stake valued at over $2 trillion, with proceeds going into a new sovereign wealth fund.
